title: Malta Year 8 Math Chapter 6 — Percentages
question: What does per cent mean, and how do you find a percentage of an amount, a sale price and a price with VAT?
intro:
Chapter 6 works with per cent: out of 100.

**Chapter 6 has four parts:**

- 6.1 Percent, fraction and decimal
- 6.2 Percentage of an amount
- 6.3 One amount as a percentage of another
- 6.4 Increase and decrease

**By the end of the chapter:**

- change between percent, fraction and decimal
- find 50%, 25%, 10%, 5% and 1% in your head
- write a score as a percentage
- work out a sale price and a price with VAT

questions.title: Percent to fraction and decimal
questions.prompt:
- **Per cent** means **out of 100**: \(25\% = \dfrac{25}{100}\).
- For a fraction, write it over 100 and simplify.
- For a decimal, divide by 100 (move the digits two places right).

**Examples:**

- **a)** \(50\%\)

- **b)** \(20\%\)

- **c)** \(75\%\)

- **d)** \(5\%\)
questions.figure_alt: A 10 by 10 grid with 25 of the 100 squares shaded: 25 out of 100 is 25%.

questions.title: Fraction or decimal to percent
questions.prompt:
- Multiply by \(100\%\).
- A fraction: make the bottom 100 first (\(\dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{60}{100}\)).
- A decimal: move the digits two places left.

**Examples:**

- **a)** \(\dfrac{3}{5}\)

- **b)** \(0.35\)

- **c)** \(\dfrac{9}{25}\)

- **d)** \(0.8\)

questions.title: Quick percentages: 50%, 25%, 10%, 1%
questions.prompt:
Four quick ones:

- \(50\%\): halve
- \(25\%\): halve, then halve again
- \(10\%\): divide by 10
- \(1\%\): divide by 100

**Examples:**

- **a)** \(50\%\) of 36 pastizzi

- **b)** \(25\%\) of €48

- **c)** \(10\%\) of 70 km

- **d)** \(1\%\) of €300

questions.title: Build it from 10%, 5% and 1%
questions.figure_alt: €40 as a bar of 10 equal parts; one part is 10% = €4, and 5% is half a part = €2.

questions.title: Any percentage: divide by 100, times the percent
questions.prompt:
\[p\% \text{ of } A = A\div100\times p\]With a calculator this works for every percentage. Without one, pick the easier order.

**Examples:**

- **a)** \(18\%\) of 50

- **b)** \(7\%\) of €200

- **c)** \(64\%\) of 25

- **d)** \(30\%\) of 45

questions.title: Out of → per cent
questions.prompt:
Write it as a fraction **part over whole**, then make the bottom 100 (or \(\times100\)).

**Examples:**

- **a)** 18 out of 25 in a test

- **b)** 12 out of 20 students walk

- **c)** 9 out of 10 goals

- **d)** 21 out of 50 seats taken
steps:
**d)** \(\times2\) top and bottom:

\[\begin{aligned} \frac{21}{50} &= \frac{42}{100} \\ &= \boxed{42\%} \end{aligned}\]

Not \(21\%\): the whole is 50, not 100.

questions.title: Sale: take the percentage off
questions.prompt:
Two steps: **find** the percentage, then **take it away** from the price.

**Examples:**

- **a)** €80 jacket, \(25\%\) off

- **b)** €45 shoes, \(10\%\) off

- **c)** €120 bike, \(15\%\) off

- **d)** €36 game, \(50\%\) off
steps:
**d)**

\[\begin{aligned} 50\% \text{ of } 36 &= 18 \\ 36 - 18 &= \boxed{18} \end{aligned}\] so €18

Not €20 for the jacket: \(20\) is the money **off**, not the new price.

questions.title: Increase: add the percentage on
questions.prompt:
- Find the percentage, then **add it** to the amount.
- In Malta, VAT is \(18\%\).

**Examples:**

- **a)** €50 + VAT \(18\%\)

- **b)** rent €200 rises by \(5\%\)

- **c)** 30 festa visitors grow by \(20\%\)

- **d)** €15 meal + \(10\%\) tip

questions.title: One step: multiply by the new percentage
questions.prompt:
After the change, the new amount is a percentage of the old one:

- up \(18\%\): \(100\% + 18\% = 118\%\), so \(\times1.18\)
- down \(25\%\): \(100\% - 25\% = 75\%\), so \(\times0.75\)

Multiply once.

**Examples:**

- **a)** €50 up \(18\%\)

- **b)** €80 down \(25\%\)

- **c)** €200 up \(5\%\)

- **d)** €40 down \(10\%\)
steps:
**d)**

\[\begin{aligned} 100\% - 10\% &= 90\% \\ 40\times0.9 &= \boxed{36} \end{aligned}\]

Not \(40\times0.1 = 4\): that is the money off, not what is left.
